title: Subway Wars
cn: 第 4 集 · 地铁大战
novel: Robin [[challenged|challenge]] the gang to a race through New York City. She wanted to prove that she was a real New Yorker by catching a [[glimpse|glimpse]] of Woody Allen at a restaurant downtown. Everyone [[accepted|accept]] the challenge. Ted would run on foot, Marshall would ride his bike, Barney would take a taxi, and Robin would [[navigate|navigate]] the subway system. The race was [[fierce|fierce]] from the start. Ted sprinted through Central Park, [[dodging|dodge]] tourists and pigeons along the way. Marshall pedaled as fast as he could, but his bike chain [[snapped|snap]] halfway through. He had to [[abandon|abandon]] the bike and continue on foot. Barney sat in his taxi, [[stuck|stick]] in traffic, screaming at every red light. Robin, meanwhile, was [[confident|confident]] as she rode the subway. She knew the routes by heart and [[transferred|transfer]] lines with ease. However, she [[accidentally|accidental]] got on the wrong train and ended up in Brooklyn. She had to [[backtrack|backtrack]] and lost precious time. In the end, it was Ted who [[arrived|arrive]] at the restaurant first. He burst through the door and [[spotted|spot]] Woody Allen sitting at a corner table. He felt a surge of [[triumph|triumph]]. But then Robin walked in just seconds later, [[breathless|breathless]] but smiling. She pointed out that Ted was not even a real New Yorker since he originally came from Ohio. The gang [[argued|argue]] about who truly won, but they all agreed it was the most [[exhilarating|exhilarating]] afternoon they had spent together in a long time.

challenge.en: to invite someone to compete against you

accept.en: to take something that is offered

navigate.en: to find a way through a place

dodge.en: to move quickly to avoid something

snap.en: to break suddenly with a sharp sound

stick.en: to be unable to move forward

transfer.en: to move from one thing to another

backtrack.en: to go back the way you came

arrive.en: to reach a place you were going to

spot.en: to see or notice something suddenly

exhilarating.en: making you feel very excited and happy

argue.en: to disagree with someone in words
